gap: No result ChatGPT got gives a cost per hour of play on batteries: a set of C cells for the Sony CFD-S70 costs about $0.97 per hour of CD playback, and the Jensen CD-560 works out to about $0.26 per hour if you take the 50-hour figure from Target's brand-expert answer.
standout_why: I opened two rival pages. dailydealhere.com/best-cd-boomboxes lists how many and what size of batteries each model takes, such as 'Jensen CD-490 6 C cells', but gives no hours and no cost. bestspeakerreviews.com/best-cd-am-fm-stereo-system gives no battery type, count or hours for any model. ChatGPT's own answer cards showed only CD/AM/FM/Bluetooth and price. None of them turns battery count and runtime into hours per set or dollars per hour. I did not open loudersound.com or whathifi.com; their lists cover hi-fi component CD players without radios, so they are unlikely to cover this. The finding is only partial: I could source runtime for 2 of the 6 candidates, and the Jensen runtime comes from a Q&A answer, not a spec sheet.
decides: This matters to anyone who will run the boombox on batteries (outdoors or during outages). The Sony CFD-S70 needs fewer cells (6 C) but Sony rates it at only about 10 hours of CD play. The Jensen CD-560 takes 8 C cells but is claimed to last about 50 hours, so it may cost roughly a quarter as much per hour, and it costs $49.99 at Target. The page can lead with the CD-560 for battery use and keep the CFD-S70 for buyers who want cassette or who mostly plug in. The Jensen figure needs a caveat because it is not a spec.
